name: ttd

relevance.justification: TTD is a curated therapeutic-target database directly covering core BioThings entity types: protein/gene targets (UniProt-identified), drugs (InChIKey/InChI/SMILES-identified small molecules and biologics), and disease indications (ICD-11 coded). It also links targets to KEGG/WikiPathways pathways and provides target-drug and target-disease relations.

novelty.justification: An older TTD snapshot (v8.1.01, 2023, ~876K records) is already deployed as 'BioThings TTD' at https://biothings.transltr.io/ttd (drug/gene/disease entity types, UniProt/ChEMBL/DrugBank identifiers) per references/pending-api-datasources.json. A separate drug-centric plugin for a later TTD release (v10.1.01, associated with the 2026 NAR update paper DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaf1154) is already recorded in built-plugins-index.md at this same 'ttd' slug/output path (agent_outputs/ttd_datasource/ttd_plugin/), covering TTD Drug ID-keyed records from P1-02/P1-03/P1-05. That prior entry's own Notes explicitly flag that target-centric records (P1-01 target info + P1-06 target-disease indications) were NOT ingested and would be 'a separate plugin' -- which is exactly the entity type and file set this evaluation targets. Target-level fields (BioChemical Class, EC number, PDB structures, function text, per-target associated-drug list, per-target ICD-11 disease indications) are not represented in the existing deployed BioThings TTD snapshot or in the drug-centric v10.1.01 plugin, so this is genuinely novel at the target-entity level even though the underlying source (TTD) is partially represented elsewhere.

openness.justification: All TTD bulk download files are served with no login, no API key, and no click-through wall from https://ttd.idrblab.cn/files/download/. License is CC BY-NC 4.0, which the evaluation-checklist explicitly treats as PASS for BioThings' non-profit academic use context (Su Lab, Scripps Research), with only a minor documented ambiguity for downstream commercial API consumers.

evidence.scope: Curated database of therapeutic protein/nucleic-acid targets and their cognate drugs, covering target identity (UniProt), target type/druggability class (Successful/Clinical trial/Preclinical/Literature-reported/Patented/Discontinued), BioChemical Class, EC number, PDB structures, function annotation, per-target list of associated drugs with clinical development status, and per-target ICD-11-coded disease indications. Also covers target-pathway (KEGG/WikiPathway) mappings and drug-level chemical structures/cross-references (evaluated separately in the pre-existing drug-centric ttd plugin).
evidence.overlap: Partial overlap with the already-deployed 'BioThings TTD' pending.api source (older v8.1.01 snapshot) and with the pre-existing drug-centric ttd_plugin (v10.1.01, DOI gkaf1154) recorded in built-plugins-index.md, which covers TTD Drug ID-keyed records only. This evaluation targets the target-centric slice (P1-01 target info + P1-06 target-disease indications) that neither prior source covers.

urls.api: No public REST/GraphQL API documented; bulk flat-file downloads only

api_info.record_coverage: full (bulk download files cover the complete current TTD release)

risks: Data volume/counts in the live v10.1.01 download files (4,298 targets) exceed the paper's reported 2024 snapshot (3,730 targets) -- TTD is continuously updated between paper publication and the live site, so the paper's counts are a lower bound, not the current total (flagged as MISMATCH in inspection).

IMPORTANT NAMING COLLISION: built-plugins-index.md already contains a '### ttd' entry (generated 2026-05-28) for a DIFFERENT paper (TTD 2026 update, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaf1154) at the identical output path agent_outputs/ttd_datasource/ttd_plugin/. That prior plugin is drug-centric (TTD Drug ID keyed, from P1-02/P1-03/P1-05). This evaluation and its resulting plugin are for the 2024 Database Issue paper (DOI 10.1093/nar/gkad751) and are target-centric (P1-01/P1-06), which the prior entry's own Notes flag as an intentionally separate, un-ingested slice. Both entries use the same 'ttd' slug -- downstream consolidation must reconcile or rename one of the two before merging pipeline_state.json.
CC BY-NC restricts commercial redistribution; acceptable for BioThings' non-profit research use per evaluation-checklist guidance, but flag for downstream commercial API consumers.
next_actions: Proceed to plugin generation (target-centric slice: P1-01 + P1-06)
